articles.title: NVIDIA is about to spend $750 billion on AI. Critics are calling it a bubble
articles.summary: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks Bloomberg AI infrastructure reporter Dina Bass about concerns over circular financing in the AI sector.
articles.titleZh: NVIDIA 即将在 AI 上投入 7500 亿美元。批评者称其为泡沫
articles.summaryZh: NPR 的 Ayesha Rascoe 向彭博社人工智能基础设施记者 Dina Bass 询问对人工智能领域循环融资的担忧。

contentParagraphs.en: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks Bloomberg AI infrastructure reporter Dina Bass about concerns over circular financing in the AI sector.
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 的 Ayesha Rascoe 向彭博社人工智能基础设施记者 Dina Bass 询问对人工智能领域循环融资的担忧。

contentParagraphs.en: AYESHA RASCOE, HOST: Seven hundred and fifty billion dollars. That's what reporters from The Information, The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg say chipmaking giant Nvidia is thinking of spending on data centers to strengthen its supply chain. And it's not just the price tag that's raising eyebrows. Dina Bass is one of the reporters with the story. She covers AI infrastructure for Bloomberg News, and she joins us now. Welcome to the program.DINA BASS: Thanks for having me.RASCOE: What other companies are involved in these talks, and how big are they as players in the AI sector?BASS: So let's start with Nvidia. They are the largest by far. They have these graphics chips that, you know, years ago they used and still do for video games and things like that. It turned out to be really important for training AI models. So it's kind of the workhorse chip in the AI space. And they are, you know, kind of using their funding and their money, their investments and their customer relationships to continue to juice demand for that.And so, you know, in the past month alone, Nvidia has unveiled a partnership with South Korean conglomerate SK Group, which means those companies will be doing more than 500 billion in business with each other. And SK owns a company called SK Hynix, which makes the memory chips whose products are critical for NVIDIA's AI chips. And also, in the last couple of days, we've reported - our sources tell us that Nvidia is in talks with OpenAI to help fund both a lease on a massive data center in Ohio and also putting those - the Nvidia chips in there and, you know, possibly other data centers.RASCOE: So who are the people kind of calling out this kind of circular financing? And explain it for the layperson - why this is circular financing.BASS: I mean, you've had, you know, Michael Burry, who's kind of famous for calling out, you know, what ended up being the - sort of the mortgage crisis. You know, a lot of reporters, a - you know, investors are looking at this as well. And the concern here ends up being - it's not just Nvidia. Nvidia's rival AMD is investing 5 billion in OpenAI's rival Anthropic. And Anthropic is then going to use AMD chips. Anthropic also has taken huge - billions of dollars of investments from Google and Amazon and agreed to use billions of dollars of their chips. And in some cases, what we're literally seeing amounts to a company giving another company money to buy its product.There's also concern that with all of the interlocking relationships, any impairment to one company risks kind of spreading a contagion throughout the whole, you know, ecosystem of all of these companies. And, you know, one of the wrinkles - you know, you have to consider that an increasing number of financial firms, so your Apollos, your Blackstones and many more, are now helping finance the, you know, billions of dollars of these large deals for data centers and chips as well.RASCOE: Yeah. So then you have financial companies also exposed.BASS: Exactly. You know, in a nutshell, the question becomes, if there's a point where the music stops on the AI expansion, you know, who ends up left without a chair? Who's left holding the bag?RASCOE: Well, how has Nvidia responded to this criticism?BASS: Look, Jensen Huang hates the term circular financing. I have personally, as have other reporters, asked him about it. You know, when I asked Jensen this question a couple months back on the day he signed an investment and sales deal with AI cloud CoreWeave, he felt that, you know, they are investing. They are juicing sales. But they are not, in his view, literally funding their own sales.RASCOE: This isn't just a concern about shareholders or workers at these companies. It's about how important these companies are to the entire U..S economy. And I should note that Anthropic, Google, Amazon and Apollo are NPR funders, just to make a note of that. But if we are seeing a bubble, like the critics say, what would be the best parallel from recent memory? Like, the dotcom bust or the meltdown over mortgage-backed securities?BASS: I covered the dotcom bubble very early in my career at Bloomberg, and there were a lot of ideas and companies that came about in that era that ended up being right. People ended up doing exactly those things. They are now major parts of, you know, the technology that we use every day - things like grocery delivery, things like location-based services, some early mobile things. But the companies behind them did not always end up being the ones that led the way for that.And you end up with a similar - you know, potentially similar situation in the AI era. People in this space will tell you AI is real. These are ideas that are happening. These are legitimate and important technologies that are going to change significant things about the way our world operates. But that doesn't necessarily translate into the notion that the companies that are currently leading each of those spaces - are currently raising a lot of money to compete in each of those spaces - those may not be the companies who, five or 10 years from now, are, you know, the ones that end up benefiting from them.RASCOE: That's Dina Bass of Bloomberg News. Thank you so much for being with us.BASS: Thank you for having me.(SOUNDBITE OF MUSIC)
contentParagraphs.zh: 艾莎·拉斯科（AYESHA RASCOE），主持人：七千五十亿美元。 《The Information》、《华尔街日报》和彭博社的记者表示，芯片制造巨头英伟达正在考虑在数据中心上投入资金，以加强其供应链。令人惊讶的不仅仅是价格标签。迪娜·巴斯是报道此事的记者之一。她为彭博新闻报道人工智能基础设施，现在加入我们。欢迎来到这个节目。 DINA BASS：感谢您邀请我。 RASCOE：还有哪些其他公司参与了这些演讲，它们作为人工智能领域的参与者有多大？BASS：那么让我们从 Nvidia 开始。它们是迄今为止最大的。他们拥有这些图形芯片，你知道，几年前他们使用并且仍然用于视频游戏和类似的东西。事实证明，这对于训练人工智能模型非常重要。所以它是人工智能领域的主力芯片。你知道，他们正在利用自己的资金、资金、投资和客户关系来继续刺激需求。因此，你知道，仅在过去一个月，Nvidia 就宣布与韩国企业集团 SK 集团建立合作伙伴关系，这意味着这些公司之间的业务量将超过 5000 亿美元。 SK 拥有一家名为 SK Hynix 的公司，该公司生产存储芯片，其产品对 NVIDIA 的 AI 芯片至关重要。而且，在过去的几天里，我们报道了 - 我们的消息来源告诉我们，Nvidia 正在与 OpenAI 进行谈判，以帮助为俄亥俄州一个大型数据中心的租赁提供资金，并将这些 - Nvidia 芯片放入其中，你知道，可能还有其他数据中心。 RASCOE：那么是谁在呼吁这种循环融资呢？并向外行解释一下为什么这是循环融资。 巴斯：我的意思是，你知道，迈克尔·伯里（Michael Burry）因大声疾呼而闻名，你知道，最终导致了抵押贷款危机。你知道，很多记者，你知道，投资者也在关注这个问题。这里的担忧最终是——不仅仅是英伟达。 Nvidia 的竞争对手 AMD 正在向 OpenAI 的竞争对手 Anthropic 投资 50 亿美元。 Anthropic 随后将使用 AMD 芯片。 Anthropic 还从谷歌和亚马逊获得了数十亿美元的巨额投资，并同意使用他们价值数十亿美元的芯片。在某些情况下，我们所看到的实际上相当于一家公司向另一家公司提供资金来购买其产品。人们还担心，由于所有这些环环相扣的关系，对一家公司的任何损害都有可能在整个生态系统中蔓延，你知道，所有这些公司。而且，你知道，其中一个问题 - 你知道，你必须考虑到越来越多的金融公司，比如阿波罗公司、黑石公司等等，现在也在为数据中心和芯片的这些大型交易提供数十亿美元的资金。 拉斯科：是的。那么金融公司也暴露了。 BASS：没错。你知道，简而言之，问题是，如果人工智能扩展中音乐到了某个点就停止了，你知道，谁最终会没有椅子？拉斯科：嗯，英伟达如何回应这种批评？巴斯：听着，黄仁勋讨厌循环融资这个词。和其他记者一样，我亲自向他询问过此事。你知道，几个月前，当我问 Jensen 这个问题时，他与 AI 云 CoreWeave 签署了投资和销售协议，他觉得，你知道，他们正在投资。他们正在推动销售。但在他看来，他们实际上并没有为自己的销售提供资金。 拉斯科：这不仅仅是这些公司股东或员工的担忧。这关系到这些公司对整个美国经济的重要性。我应该指出，Anthropic、谷歌、亚马逊和阿波罗都是 NPR 的资助者，只是为了说明这一点。但如果我们看到泡沫，就像批评者所说的那样，那么最近记忆中最好的相似之处是什么？比如，互联网泡沫破灭还是抵押贷款支持证券的崩溃？巴斯：我在彭博社职业生涯的早期就报道了互联网泡沫，那个时代出现了很多想法和公司，但最终都被证明是正确的。人们最终确实做了那些事情。你知道，它们现在是我们每天使用的技术的主要组成部分——比如杂货配送、基于位置的服务、一些早期的移动设备。但他们背后的公司并不总是最终成为引领这一趋势的公司。而且你最终会遇到类似的——你知道，在人工智能时代可能会出现类似的情况。这个领域的人们会告诉你人工智能是真实的。这些都是正在发生的想法。这些都是合法且重要的技术，将彻底改变我们世界的运作方式。但这并不一定意味着目前在每个领域处于领先地位的公司正在筹集大量资金以在每个领域进行竞争，这些公司可能不会是五年或十年后最终从中受益的公司。 拉斯科：这是彭博新闻社的迪娜·巴斯。非常感谢你和我们在一起。BASS：谢谢你有我。（音乐原声）

articles.title: It may be easier to get your first mortgage than you think - here's why
articles.summary: More relaxed mortgage regulation opens the door for some first-time buyers, but it comes with risk.
articles.titleZh: 获得第一笔抵押贷款可能比您想象的更容易 - 这就是原因
articles.summaryZh: 更宽松的抵押贷款监管为一些首次购房者打开了大门，但它也伴随着风险。

contentParagraphs.en: Image source, Getty ImagesByCost of living correspondentUpdated 1 hour agoIf you're working towards buying your first home you might feel like everything is stacked against you - but recent changes could help you get a mortgage.It hard to save for a deposit when the cost of living is so high, the average house price is nearly £300,000, external and interest rates on new mortgages are rising.However, a rule change and more flexible lending mean first-time buyers can now borrow up to six, or at the most, seven times what you earn in a year.This means mortgages will be within reach for more people but it is a shift that comes with some risk so here's what you need to know.The backgroundReckless mortgage lending was blamed for the financial crisis of 2008, which brought some banks to their knees and saw people lose their homes.In 2014, the business secretary of the time, Vince Cable, said he was appalled that some mortgage providers were lending five times a mortgage applicant's income, suggesting a stable level was up to 3.5 times.But house prices have risen significantly since, outstripping wage rises most of the time. So a bigger loan has become the only option for many potential buyers.Regulation limited how much lenders were able to lend - technically, only 15% of their new mortgages could be at higher than 4.5 times loan-to-income. Many of the big lenders played it very safe meaning they didn't get close to the limit.The changeBut those rules have been relaxed, external over the last year. Many lenders are offering bigger loans compared with your income, with niche lenders and building societies at the highest end."The greater flexibility could mean that first time buyers that felt ownership was still out of reach may find that the amount they can borrow has changed markedly in a relatively short time," says David Hollingworth, of mortgage broker L&C.The idea of taking a big income stretch is not going to be for everyone, says Aaron Strutt, of broker Trinity Financial."But it is tempting for many because it gives them the option to get out of renting or living with parents," he adds.What you needThere are still strict criteria you most likely need to meet as a first-time buyer to be offered a larger mortgage. They may include:A good credit history with limited credit card debt and loans and no missed paymentsA regular salary, ruling out many who are self-employedA salary large enough to qualify for specific mortgages, which varies depending on the borrower and the lenderAn acceptance to borrow at a certain interest rate usually for five or 10 years, rather than twoEnough savings to offer a deposit, although the options for low-deposit mortgages have increased tooAlso, circumstances can change, such as what is on offer when you come to renew or shop around for another mortgage after five years. Lenders may become more picky if the economic outlook takes a turn for the worse.Personal circumstances can change too, such as losing a job, having to take time out to care for a loved one, or illness of your own."Ideally you need to have a cash buffer or a plan in case something happens financially," says Strutt.Get in touchAre you affected by issues covered in this story?

articles.summary: A defunct part of a Falcon 9 rocket could slam into the moon at more than 5,000 miles per hour, according to scientists.

articles.title: What would it take to get peptides on the shelf?
articles.summary: An FDA advisory panel recently voted to green-light some popular peptides. The decision brought enormous attention to the market for these products — and concerns about the unregulated supply.
articles.titleZh: 怎样才能让肽上架？
articles.summaryZh: FDA 的一个顾问小组最近投票批准了一些流行的肽。这一决定引起了这些产品市场的巨大关注，以及对供应不受监管的担忧。

contentParagraphs.en: The popular and experimental drugs called peptides received unprecedented attention last month during a marathon hearing held by a panel that advises the Food and Drug Administration.
contentParagraphs.zh: 上个月，在一个为美国食品和药物管理局提供咨询的小组举行的马拉松式听证会上，一种名为肽的流行实验性药物受到了前所未有的关注。

contentParagraphs.en: Catherine Falls Commercial/Getty Images
contentParagraphs.zh: 凯瑟琳瀑布商业/盖蒂图片社

contentParagraphs.en: Catherine Falls Commercial/Getty Images
contentParagraphs.zh: 凯瑟琳瀑布商业/盖蒂图片社

contentParagraphs.en: The peptide saga has reached what could be its most confusing chapter — at least for consumers.
contentParagraphs.zh: 肽传奇已经到了可能是最令人困惑的一章——至少对消费者来说是这样。

contentParagraphs.en: The popular — and experimental — drugs received unprecedented attention in late July during a marathon hearing held by a panel that advises the Food and Drug Administration.
contentParagraphs.zh: 7月下旬，在一个为食品和药物管理局提供咨询的小组举行的马拉松式听证会上，这种受欢迎的实验性药物受到了前所未有的关注。

contentParagraphs.en: The panel considered whether to back the production of seven different peptide therapies — and voted in favor of all but one — despite concerns raised by the agency's own scientists.
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管该机构自己的科学家提出了担忧，但该小组考虑了是否支持七种不同肽疗法的生产，并投票赞成除一种之外的所有疗法。

contentParagraphs.en: These peptides include some of the most sought-after injectables, BPC-157, TB-500 and MOTS-c.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这些肽包括一些最受欢迎的注射剂：BPC-157、TB-500 和 MOTS-c。

contentParagraphs.en: But that recommendation alone doesn't change the status of these substances. It's still illegal for pharmacies in the U.S. to make these compounds.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但仅该建议并不能改变这些物质的状态。在美国，药房生产这些化合物仍然是非法的。

contentParagraphs.en: The FDA staff and leadership now need to review the data and decide whether compounding pharmacies in the U.S. should be allowed to make any of the seven peptides the panel considered.
contentParagraphs.zh: FDA 工作人员和领导层现在需要审查数据并决定是否应允许美国的复合药房生产专家组考虑的七种肽中的任何一种。

contentParagraphs.en: It's a regulatory nuance that Dr. Jessica Duncan, who spoke in favor of peptides at the FDA meeting, now finds herself explaining to patients who've seen the headlines and want to know when these therapies will be available.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这是一个监管上的细微差别，杰西卡·邓肯博士在 FDA 会议上发言支持肽，现在她正在向那些看到头条新闻并想知道这些疗法何时可用的患者解释。

contentParagraphs.en: "They are now even more curious," says Duncan, chief medical officer for the telehealth company IVIM Health. "We tell them that the timeline is uncertain."
contentParagraphs.zh: “他们现在更好奇了，”远程医疗公司 IVIM Health 的首席医疗官邓肯说。 “我们告诉他们时间表是不确定的。”

contentParagraphs.en: What are the chances these peptides get the green light?
contentParagraphs.zh: 这些肽获得批准的机会有多大？

contentParagraphs.en: There's no guarantee, but it seems likely the FDA will move forward. The agency usually follows its advisory committees' recommendations.
contentParagraphs.zh: 虽然不能保证，但 FDA 很可能会继续推进。该机构通常遵循其咨询委员会的建议。

contentParagraphs.en: Plus, there's high demand for these products — and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., whose agency oversees the FDA, has called to make them available.
contentParagraphs.zh: 此外，对这些产品的需求量很大，负责监督 FDA 的卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F. Kennedy Jr.) 已呼吁提供这些产品。

contentParagraphs.en: Normally, the agency would move forward through its formal rulemaking process, which could take anywhere from several months to possibly over a year, says Jesse Dresser, a partner at the law firm Frier Levitt who represents compounding pharmacies and others in the industry.
contentParagraphs.zh: Frier Levitt 律师事务所合伙人杰西·德莱瑟 (Jesse Dresser) 表示，通常情况下，该机构将完成正式的规则制定流程，这可能需要几个月到一年多的时间，他代表复方药房和业内其他机构。

contentParagraphs.en: "It would actually surprise me if this followed the traditional pathway of formal rulemaking," Dresser told NPR. "Whatever options exist to make this a faster process, I think they are going to be leveraged."
contentParagraphs.zh: 德莱瑟告诉美国国家公共广播电台：“如果这遵循正式规则制定的传统途径，我实际上会感到惊讶。” “无论有什么选择可以使这一过程变得更快，我认为它们都将得到利用。”

contentParagraphs.en: One likely scenario: The agency could green-light these peptides in the interim by placing them on what's known as the "Category One list."
contentParagraphs.zh: 一种可能的情况是：该机构可以暂时批准这些肽，将它们列入所谓的“一类清单”。

contentParagraphs.en: That would give compounding pharmacies cover to begin making these products sooner, while the longer rulemaking process plays out.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这将使复合药房有能力更快地开始生产这些产品，同时更长的规则制定过程也将结束。

contentParagraphs.en: "I do think that there is significant pressure here, but the FDA needs to follow the data," says Ilisa Bernstein, a former FDA official and pharmacist who's an expert on drug and pharmacy policy.
contentParagraphs.zh: “我确实认为这里存在很大的压力，但 FDA 需要跟踪数据，” FDA 前官员和药剂师、药品和药房政策专家伊丽莎·伯恩斯坦 (Ilisa Bernstein) 说。

contentParagraphs.en: Want the latest stories on the science of healthy living? Subscribe to NPR's Health newsletter.
contentParagraphs.zh: 想了解健康生活科学的最新故事吗？订阅 NPR 的健康通讯。

contentParagraphs.en: Another route — one that would almost certainly result in a legal challenge — is that Kennedy could cite the dangers posed by the unregulated peptide market as a rationale to immediately place these on a list that OKs their compounding, says Dresser.
contentParagraphs.zh: 德莱瑟说，另一条路线——几乎肯定会导致法律挑战——是肯尼迪可以引用不受监管的肽市场带来的危险作为理由，立即将这些产品列入可以进行复合的清单中。

contentParagraphs.en: That authority is normally used to remove unsafe products from the market, not fast-track them. But "this is a unique scenario, unique product, unique industry and unique administration," he says.
contentParagraphs.zh: 该权力通常用于将不安全的产品从市场上剔除，而不是快速跟踪它们。但“这是一个独特的场景、独特的产品、独特的行业和独特的管理，”他说。

contentParagraphs.en: The agency could also buck the recommendations of the panel and decide not to change the status of these peptides. That would likely result in lawsuits from the industry, says Abha Kundi, an attorney at Aaron Fox Schiff who focuses on FDA regulatory law.
contentParagraphs.zh: 该机构还可以违背专家组的建议，决定不改变这些肽的状态。 Aaron Fox Schiff 律师事务所专注于 FDA 监管法的律师 Abha Kundi 表示，这可能会导致业界提起诉讼。

contentParagraphs.en: Though she adds that the agency is clearly "very attuned" to dealing with the real world landscape and the current availability of these products.
contentParagraphs.zh: 不过她补充说，该机构显然“非常适应”处理现实世界的情况和这些产品的当前可用性。

contentParagraphs.en: "In many ways, the toothpaste is out of the tube here. I think that is absolutely part of the calculus."
contentParagraphs.zh: “从很多方面来说，牙膏都是从管子里出来的。我认为这绝对是微积分的一部分。”

contentParagraphs.en: Why have peptides become so controversial?
contentParagraphs.zh: 为什么肽变得如此有争议？

contentParagraphs.en: Demand for them has leapfrogged well ahead of the evidence.
contentParagraphs.zh: 对它们的需求远远超过了证据。

contentParagraphs.en: They are promoted widely in the wellness and longevity space and often taken together by injection as "stacks," for injury recovery, muscle growth and fat loss, improving athletic performance, enhancing metabolism and more.
contentParagraphs.zh: 它们在健康和长寿领域得到广泛推广，通常通过注射“堆叠”的方式组合在一起，用于损伤恢复、肌肉生长和脂肪减少、提高运动表现、增强新陈代谢等。

contentParagraphs.en: Unlike many of the GLP-1 weight-loss drugs — which are also synthetic peptides — none of the seven peptides under consideration has undergone the kind of large-scale, rigorous trials in humans that are necessary for drug approval.
contentParagraphs.zh: 与许多 GLP-1 减肥药物（也是合成肽）不同，正在考虑的七种肽都没有经过药物批准所需的大规模、严格的人体试验。

contentParagraphs.en: But the gray market exploded several years ago, after the FDA placed many of them on a list that prohibited compounding pharmacies from making them due to safety concerns.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但几年前，由于安全问题，美国食品和药物管理局将其中许多药物列入禁止复合药房生产的清单后，灰色市场爆发了。

contentParagraphs.en: That dynamic has led to a dangerous situation. People are now obtaining these peptides from unvetted sources under the guise that they're only being used for "research purposes" — not for human consumption.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这种动态导致了危险的局面。人们现在从未经审查的来源获取这些肽，其幌子是它们仅用于“研究目的”，而不是用于人类消费。

contentParagraphs.en: "The gray market space is a lot seedier than what people think," says Dr. Haleem Mohammed, chief medical officer for Gameday Men's Health, which operates health clinics that offer hormone optimization and peptides. "That's nowhere I want my patients getting their medications from."
contentParagraphs.zh: “灰色市场空间比人们想象的要肮脏得多，”Gameday Men's Health 的首席医疗官 Haleem Mohammed 博士说，该公司经营提供激素优化和肽的健康诊所。 “我不希望我的病人从那里获得药物。”

contentParagraphs.en: Mohammed was one of the FDA panelists who voted in favor of these peptides. Like others in the industry, he argues that the agency's presentation during the meeting did not showcase the full breadth of evidence.
contentParagraphs.zh: 穆罕默德是 FDA 小组成员之一，投票支持这些肽。与业内其他人一样，他认为该机构在会议期间的演示并未展示全部证据。

contentParagraphs.en: "This is not a rubber stamp," he told NPR. "This is about moving towards a regulated pathway for peptides that patients are already using."
contentParagraphs.zh: “这不是橡皮图章，”他告诉美国国家公共广播电台。 “这是为了朝着患者已经使用的肽的受监管途径迈进。”

contentParagraphs.en: The FDA's scientists raised numerous concerns about the lack of published human data for all seven of the peptides and recommended against allowing for their production.
contentParagraphs.zh: FDA 的科学家对所有七种肽缺乏已发表的人体数据提出了许多担忧，并建议不要允许生产它们。

contentParagraphs.en: Even defining each substance proved difficult because the common name for a peptide can cover many compounds with quite different chemical compositions in the scientific literature, they said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他们说，即使定义每种物质也很困难，因为肽的通用名称可以涵盖科学文献中化学成分完全不同的许多化合物。

contentParagraphs.en: Legitimizing these peptides for compounding doesn't require nearly the same degree of evidence as FDA drug approval, but
contentParagraphs.zh: 使这些肽的合成合法化并不需要与 FDA 药物批准几乎相同程度的证据，但是

articles.title: Stock market turmoil sheds stark light on the opaque AI economy
articles.summary:
Investors scramble to make sense of a shock Chinese challenge to the dominance of western chipmakers
Even for the rollercoaster world of AI, last week was particularly volatile as investors scrambled to keep up with developments that threatened the dominance of the largest wester
articles.titleZh: 股市动荡凸显了不透明的人工智能经济
articles.summaryZh:
投资者争相理解中国对西方芯片制造商主导地位的令人震惊的挑战
即使对于像过山车一样的人工智能世界来说，上周的波动也尤为剧烈，因为投资者争先恐后地跟上威胁到西方最大人工智能主导地位的事态发展。

contentParagraphs.en: Even for the rollercoaster world of AI, last week was particularly volatile as investors scrambled to keep up with developments that threatened the dominance of the largest western chipmakers.It began with a double whammy. On Monday, the Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT floated on the Shanghai stock market, soaring by 466% in value to 3.3tn yuan (£365bn).That same day, it was reported that China had developed its own tools to carry out deep-ultraviolet lithography, a technique essential to the computer chip supply chain over which the Dutch company ASML had held a monopoly.AI-linked shares, particularly chipmakers, dropped around the world, sending many indices sliding. South Korea’s main share index, the Kospi, fell 11.5% on Tuesday and a further 6% on Wednesday, dragged down by its two biggest companies – the semiconductor maker SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics.On Thursday, the main US tech index, the Nasdaq, fell into correction territory at one point after dropping more than 10% from its recent high, before easing back. Nvidia lost more than 5% by Thursday evening, by which time it had been overtaken by Apple as the world’s largest listed company.The next day there was a big rebound, when strong financial results from Amazon and Microsoft calmed traders’ nerves. The Kospi jumped nearly 20% – although the week’s slump still means it recorded its worst month since the height of the global financial crisis in October 2008.So, what exactly do these advances mean, and why have they got western investors so jittery?CXMT’s debut is impressive. But the company is arguably more of a boon to the global AI economy than a threat. It makes dynamic random-access memory (Dram) chips, which store the data that other AI chips draw on for their calculations.There is a global shortage of Dram chips, which is why phones and computers are expected to get far more expensive. Crucially, they are not graphics processing units (GPUs) – which are the key chips and the “brains” in an AI system.This means, put simply, that CXMT is not a threat to GPU maker Nvidia, the biggest company in the AI economy and the only one making a profit on AI. They produce complementary, not competing goods.China’s president, Xi Jinping, speaks at the opening of the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Beijing. China is making rapid advances in the semiconductors used to drive AI. Photograph: Greg Baker/AFP/Getty ImagesThe Chinese company could be a threat to SK Hynix and Micron, which do make memory chips. However, Alvin Nguyen, an analyst at the research firm Forrester, said the sell-off in these shares was an “overreaction” given that the global memory chip shortage is likely to continue until 2030.“SK Hynix, Micron, others, they can’t produce enough memory chips to begin with … the demand keeps growing even higher,” Nguyen said.A more serious concern could be the news that China can make the lithography tools. These are essentially extremely precise lasers that allow chipmakers to etch the thinnest lines in the world into wafers of silicon.Until now, only ASML could manufacture such machines. If this week’s reports are correct, Beijing could – in theory – produce GPUs that rival Nvidia’s. This would spell trouble for the world’s biggest company, and therefore Wall Street. But a serious competitor is still years away.“Fabs [semiconductor fabrication plants], as I know them, still take years to develop,” said Nguyen.Mark Boost, the chief executive of the UK cloud company Civo, agreed. “Investors are overreacting to the short-term threat,” he said. “Manufacturing a handful of [deep-ultraviolet] machines is a massive symbolic victory, but not a commercial replacement for ASML overnight.skip past newsletter promotionafter newsletter promotion“Fabs run on efficiency and yield, and until these Chinese tools can match western reliability, ASML’s global dominance remains structurally safe outside mainland China.”Long term, this week’s advances are gamechanging for the AI economy, although in many ways they should have been predictable. Given US export controls, China has had little choice but to develop domestic capabilities.Chris Beauchamp, the chief market analyst at IG, an online share trading company, said: “These Chinese chip companies appear poised to do to the big chipmakers what they have done to steel, automobiles and a host of other industries, namely undercut them and outcompete them on price.”It may be that last week’s correction is an overreaction – but also a reasonable response to a circular and extremely opaque AI economy that rests heavily on the fate of a single company, Nvidia.Its shares are gradually creeping up again, although they are still below what they were last week. A contributing factor to the investor skittishness appears to be yet another circular, opaque deal.Last Sunday, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia was considering providing a $250bn (£186bn) backstop to OpenAI for a large datacentre project. This comes roughly half a year after a $100bn deal between the two companies fell apart.It was a significant factor in Nvidia’s decline over the week, according to Morningstar. The anxiety that underlies this is that the company has become the “central bank of AI” – holding up vast parts of the economy, and the global stock market, in ways that most people, investors included, do not understand.Many believe that it cannot last. What is on the other side is less clear.“Nvidia knows the gravy train’s going to run out,” Nguyen said. “Everybody’s waiting for them to fall apart. I don’t know that they will because what they do still has value … at some point in the future, they’ll no longer be one of the most valuable companies in the world. Maybe … they’ll be worth only $2tn. It’s still pretty good.”

articles.title: US and Japan take action to prop up yen in rare joint move
articles.summary: Both countries have said that they will not hesitate to conduct joint interventions in the future.
articles.titleZh: 美国和日本罕见联合采取行动支撑日元
articles.summaryZh: 两国均表示未来将毫不犹豫地进行联合干预。

contentParagraphs.en: Japan and the US have confirmed that they jointly intervened last week to halt a slide in the yen after it fell to a fresh 40-year low.The joint intervention is the first since 2011, when both countries took coordinated action to weaken the yen after the devastating earthquake and tsunami that hit eastern Japan.Both Japan's Ministry of Finance and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have said that they will not hesitate to conduct more joint interventions in the future.It highlights both countries' efforts to prevent a sell-off in the yen and Japanese government bonds from having an impact on the global economy, including potentially helping to push up borrowing costs for Washington.Bank of Japan data indicated that Tokyo may have sold almost $59bn of US dollars to buy yen when it intervened in New York markets on Thursday, before Friday's confirmed joint intervention with Washington.The US has not confirmed the size of its intervention, but a Reuters photograph of a notepad in front of Bessent during a cabinet meeting on Friday read: "To Do: Buy Japanese Yen $5-10 bil".Shigeto Nagai, head of Japan economics at Oxford Economics, told the BBC: "The United States agreed to participate in the coordinated intervention because it serves its national interests by offering the prospect of significant benefits at a low cost."The two countries are expected to continue to intervene "intermittently in a coordinated manner for some time", he added."Even if the actual amount of intervention is not particularly large, the prolonged sense of vigilance regarding intervention will be effective in deterring speculators." The yen is historically weak mainly due to Japan having much lower central bank interest rates than other major economies like the US. That makes the Japanese currency less attractive to international investors.The Bank of Japan last raised interest rates in June, as it increased its main rate to 1% - the highest level since September 1995. In comparison, the US Federal Reserve's benchmark rate is in a range of 3.50% to 3.75%.Japan also faces other issues including a decades-long slide in its working-age population, low productivity and a heavy reliance on energy imports that are priced in US dollars.On Monday, Japan's finance ministry said Friday's intervention with the US Treasury Department "countered excessive volatility and disorderly movements in the Japanese yen in recent months".The "coordinated foreign exchange actions countered disorderly yen movements," Bessent said in a social media post."We strongly support Japan's decisive market and monetary steps to correct the substantial undervaluation of the yen," he added."They have a weakening yen, and they wanted a little bit of help. And we're always there for Japan," US President Donald Trump told reporters on Sunday.The dollar fell by 0.2% to 157.07 yen after Trump's comments, well off the 40-year high of 164 last month, but rose back to 157.70 yen after the Japanese finance ministry's statement.Additional reporting by Osmond Chia

articles.title: 'You can't describe the loss' - the reality of bovine TB on farmers
articles.summary: Wildlife intervention proposals are controversial but farmers say they are needed to reduce bTB.
articles.titleZh: “你无法描述损失”——牛结核病对农民的现实
articles.summaryZh: 野生动物干预提案存在争议，但农民表示需要这些提案来减少 bTB。

contentParagraphs.en: The effects bovine TB (bTB) has on farmers ranges from emotional to financial.Breeder Rachel Leader said the loss of cattle "has a devastating effect on all of the family"."The loss of that one animal, or animals, that you've grown up with, and suddenly there's nothing after these years of generation... it's just mind boggling, and you can't describe the loss when you do lose your cattle."But what can be done to tackle bTB?A 12-week consultation, launched in early July by Northern Ireland's agriculture,
contentParagraphs.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

contentParagraphs.en: environment and rural affairs minister, is asking for views on wildlife interventions and explores options such as culling badgers or testing and vaccinating or removing them.The cost of dealing with the disease is expected to exceed £70m this year, the bulk of it in compensation to farmers.While the rate of bTB has fallen lately, it is still close to 10% of the national herd.The consultation is part of the Blueprint for Bovine TB Eradication launched last year.The Chief Veterinary Officer Brian Dooher said the disease was a "complex problem", requiring a "comprehensive and evidence-based approach".Rachel Leader said she plans to respond to the consultation."They blame badgers, but there are other elements that I'm sure will cause and contribute. I don't think there's enough traceability."Speaking at the Clogher Valley Show in County Tyrone, Leader said she had one heifer "that was taken away 18 months ago".She said after going through tests for bTB her heifer "was actually clear". "It's the impact of losing pedigree Herefords, the family line, the genetic breeding that we've had to build up. She would have been one of our show animals for Balmoral, so we were devastated at that loss."We do have a replacement heifer of hers. But very often, when you've had generations of breeding cattle, breeding the family lines... to lose those and then try and start again. It just doesn't work." Wildlife intervention involves actions to tackle the maintenance and spread of bTB in badgers, which are implicated in the spread of the disease. A previous order by former minister Edwin Poots for a cull of badgers was quashed by the High Court. The current agriculture, environment and rural affairs minister Andrew Muir ordered a review of the department's bTB strategy which was delivered in 2024. A steering group was then formed and published a blueprint for eradication last year. Muir said bTB continued to have "a devastating impact" on farmers, their families and rural communities. "It also places unsustainable costs on both industry and government."The Blueprint to eradicate bTB sets out three key pillars on which action is required to tackle this problem; Cattle, People and Wildlife. "I recognise that a wildlife intervention is a complex and sensitive issue, and one on which there are strongly held and differing views."He added that there was "no preferred option" in the consultation.

articles.titleZh: 昂山素季2.5年来首次确认与外界接触，看上去很健康
articles.summaryZh: 缅甸军政府最新发布的照片​​显示昂山素季会见红十字国际委员会官员。

contentParagraphs.en: Detained Burmese leader Aung San Suu Kyi has been allowed to meet a delegation from the International Committee of the Red Cross, the first confirmed outside contact with her since a letter to her son two and a half years ago.In photographs of the meeting released by the military government Suu Kyi appeared to be healthy.She was detained shortly after the armed forces deposed her government in 2021, and sentenced to 33 years in jail on what are widely viewed as trumped-up charges, though her sentence has been reduced and she has been moved to house arrest.Despite repeated assurances from the military that Suu Kyi is alive and well, they have never provided any convincing evidence of this.Her son Kim Aris has in recent months mounted an international campaign demanding proof of life for the 81-year-old democracy icon.Now a delegation from the ICRC has been allowed to meet her – her first confirmed meeting with anyone outside the government for nearly four years.Photographs released of her with the ICRC team led by its representative Arnaud de Baecque show Suu Kyi looking relaxed and well, although no details of her state of health have been given, nor of what they talked about."The visit was carried out in accordance with the ICRC's standards and procedures for visiting people deprived of liberty. This included the opportunity to speak with Daw Aung San Suu Kyi in private," the ICRC said in a short statement.Kim Aris welcomed the news, saying it was the first positive development for his mother in more than five years. "This may be a first step, but it must not be the last," he said in a post on social media.
contentParagraphs.zh: 被拘留的缅甸领导人昂山素季获准会见红十字国际委员会的代表团，这是自两年半前给她儿子写信以来首次确认与她有外部接触。在军政府公布的会面照片中，昂山素季似乎很健康。2021年武装部队推翻政府后不久，她就被拘留，并因被广泛认为捏造的罪名被判处 33 年监禁，尽管她的判决已被减刑，她已被软禁。尽管军方一再保证昂山素季还活着，身体健康，但他们从未提供任何令人信服的证据。最近几个月，她的儿子金·阿里斯发起了一场国际运动，要求提供这位81岁民主偶像的生命证明。现在，红十字国际委员会的一个代表团获准会见她——近四年来，她首次确认与政府以外的任何人会面。她与红十字国际委员会代表领导的团队的照片被公布在阿尔诺·德巴克的镜头下，昂山素季看起来很轻松、健康，但没有透露她的健康状况以及他们谈论的内容。红十字国际委员会在一份简短的声明中表示：“这次探视是按照红十字国际委员会探视被剥夺自由者的标准和程序进行的。其中包括与昂山素季私下交谈的机会。”金阿里斯对这一消息表示欢迎，称这是他母亲五年多以来的第一个积极进展。 “这可能是第一步，但绝不能是最后一步，”他在社交媒体上发帖称。

articles.titleZh: 英国国家投资机构遭遇数据泄露
articles.summaryZh:
安全漏洞导致 51 名政府官员的敏感信息和联系方式暴露 40 小时
在一次数据泄露导致“高层管理信息”泄露后，负责英国国家投资的公共机构被迫改善其内部安全。

contentParagraphs.en: The public body in charge of the UK’s state investments has been pushed to improve its internal security after a data breach left “high-level management information” publicly accessible for nearly two days.UK Government Investments (UKGI), the agency that manages the taxpayers’ interest in a swathe of companies including Channel 4 and the Post Office, said the security failure also left more than 50 government officials’ personal details exposed for nearly 40 hours.The state body, best known for managing government holdings in bailed-out lenders Royal Bank of Scotland and Lloyds after the 2008 financial crisis, blamed the breach on an unnamed staff member who it said failed to follow security rules.“An internal file containing high-level management information and the names and work email addresses of 51 government officials was publicly accessible for [about] 40 hours, following the actions of a member of staff who did not follow established information security policies,” UKGI said in its annual report.It stopped short of divulging the date of the security failure but said it had been identified within the past financial year, after which it was escalated to board members and also to the UK’s information watchdog, the Information Commissioner’s Office.Bosses also hired external experts to review security protocols, who suggested the body “strengthen our controls and incident preparedness”.“The overwhelming majority of which UKGI has since implemented or will be implementing in the coming months,” UKGI said.The incident will be a wake-up call for public agencies, at a time when the rapid rise of AI has prompted fresh fears over how the frontier technology could exploit security gaps.Open AI recently said that a rogue AI agent – an autonomous tool able to carry out sequences of commands without human help – had located and used logins to access four unnamed “publicly available services” in addition to the US startup Hugging Face, a company that hosts a database of AI models.skip past newsletter promotionafter newsletter promotionHugging Face said a human attacker could have found and exploited the same flaws, but the difference was the sheer scale of the agent’s attempts to find a way through. “Agents bring a steep increase in the number of paths an attacker can test, the speed at which failed paths can be replaced, and the volume of evidence defenders must interpret,” it added.

articles.title: New Spider-Man film sees second-biggest ever global opening weekend
articles.summary: The strong box office performance gives a boost to Disney ahead of the much-anticipated Avengers: Doomsday.
articles.titleZh: 新蜘蛛侠电影迎来有史以来第二大的全球首映周末
articles.summaryZh: 强劲的票房表现为迪士尼在万众期待的《复仇者联盟：世界末日》之前提供了动力。

contentParagraphs.en: Spider-Man: Brand New Day brought in $927m (£687m) of global ticket sales to make it the second-biggest opening weekend ever as it shot past its estimated $225m production budget.The superhero movie - starring real-life husband and wife Tom Holland and Zendaya - is only behind Avengers: Endgame, which took in more than $1.2bn in its opening weekend in 2019.Brand New Day also set a second-best North American record, with box office takings of $335m.The film's strong performance gives a much-needed boost for Marvel Studios ahead of the highly-anticipated December release of Avengers: Doomsday, after a string of Marvel movies under-performed in recent years.Brand New Day, which opened in cinemas last week, picks up a few years after 2021's Spider-Man: No Way Home as Peter Parker continues to fight crime in a world that has forgotten he is the masked superhero.The latest instalment of the hugely popular franchise received largely positive reviews, with some calling it Holland's best Spider-Man performance yet.Brand New Day made $572m from more than 73,000 screens outside the US, including $121m from China, distributor Sony Pictures said. That included $49m in UK ticket sales over the weekend.Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige said the opening of Brand New Day was "truly phenomenal", adding that he was grateful to audiences for "coming out and experiencing our film the way it was meant to be seen."The film is Marvel's last big-screen outing before Doomsday, the long-awaited culmination of multiple superhero story arcs after Avengers: Endgame.Marvel films released since Endgame have struggled to attract the same broad audiences as they did at their peak.Big budget films like The Marvels and Thunderbolts recouped their production costs but were among the studio's lowest-grossing films.Spider-Man remains one of Marvel's most lucrative franchises, with No Way Home making nearly $2bn in ticket sales.Cinema attendance has slowed since the Covid-19 pandemic, which accelerated the shift to home-streaming options like Netflix.But the big screen has staged something of a comeback this year, with the North American box office takings on track to pass $10bn for the first time since 2019.That was helped by blockbuster hits by including Toy Story 5, Michael, and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie - which have made more than $1bn each.July releases Brand New Day and The Odyssey - director Christopher Nolan's take on the epic Greek poem - are also on track to top the $1bn mark.Indie horror flicks Obsession and Backrooms emerged as surprise successes, bringing in more than $390m each despite their modest budgets.

articles.title: Israel defies Trump’s peace plan as it escalates deadly attacks on Gaza
articles.summary: Israel escalates Gaza attacks and pushes hardline demands, threatening the US-backed peace roadmap.
articles.titleZh: 以色列无视特朗普的和平计划，升级对加沙的致命袭击
articles.summaryZh: 以色列升级对加沙的袭击并提出强硬要求，威胁到美国支持的和平路线图。

contentParagraphs.en: Israeli forces have intensified their military operations in the Gaza Strip since the roadmap for a second stage of the Palestinian enclave’s “ceasefire” was announced last week.United States President Donald Trump described Hamas’s acceptance of the Gaza deal as a monumental step towards security and stability.In Gaza, the reality is very different, with at least 19 Palestinians killed on Saturday in Israeli attacks, bringing the weekend death toll to 26 people, including women and children.Despite Hamas agreeing to a phased disarmament, Israel’s government says it has “serious security concerns” about the plan, and there has been strong resistance from Israeli politicians to the deal.The continued bombardment of Gaza, contributing to Israel’s continued breaches of October’s “ceasefire” agreement, will likely threaten Trump’s peace plan and exacerbate the already dire humanitarian situation for Palestinians in the enclave.Sudden deathThere has been a huge uptick in attacks in Gaza since the Trump announcement.This stands in stark contrast to the diplomatic progress heralded by Washington. The Board of Peace and the International Stabilization Force (ISF), which are intended to manage post-war Gaza, had announced an agreement to implement the next phase of the “ceasefire” based on a detailed 15-point roadmap.While Hamas formally accepted the document, questions have been raised as to whether Palestinian factions might eventually walk away due to continuous Israeli attacks on Gaza.Eyad al-Qarra, a Palestinian political analyst based in Gaza, told Al Jazeera that this step would be an uncalculated risk for Hamas and other Palestinian groups.“There is still hope that the factions will not reach this stage. Otherwise, it is feared that the price would be even higher, as Israel would exploit this to launch an even wider war on Gaza,” al-Qarra said.“It is vital for the factions not to give Israel any pretext or excuse to make it appear as though both sides are equally responsible for the failure.”The weapons pretextRather than embracing the roadmap, the Israeli government has actively worked to impose stringent new parameters.Israeli media have reported that the government is demanding the total disarmament of Hamas and that weapons be handed over to a Western state. They also insist that no Palestinian entity plays a role in managing the disarmament process.Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office, said Israeli forces would not withdraw until the complete demilitarisation of Hamas, which further complicates the process.“The priority for Hamas and other factions today is relieving the population, not restoring weapons or military workshops,” al-Qarra said.“However, while the factions agreed to limit these weapons under international or regional oversight to stop the war, they will never legitimise the complete elimination of the concept of Palestinian resistance.”Electoral manoeuvresExperts point to deep-seated domestic political calculations in Netanyahu’s opaque stance on the Gaza issue, particularly given that the general elections are due in October.Mtanes Shehadeh, an expert on Israeli affairs, observed that the government is treating the Gaza understandings strictly as a tactical manoeuvre.“Israel seeks to continue the killing, starvation and siege in the Strip, and to obstruct any actual, practical progress in the second phase of the agreement, without explicitly announcing its rejection of the roadmap,” Shehadeh stated.Palestinian residents salvage what they can from an apartment targeted in overnight Israeli attack in Gaza City on August 2, 2026 [Omar Al-Qataa/ AFP]Netanyahu is also attempting to avoid a public clash with Trump by appeasing him, possibly by allowing limited increases in aid into Gaza while stalling on core issues such as the military withdrawal.“The government of Benjamin Netanyahu will continue its policy of procrastination, evasion, and disruption until the date of the Israeli elections on October 27, because any serious implementation of the agreed-upon roadmap will lead to electoral damage for Netanyahu,” Shehadeh added.Political analyst Ahmed al-Hila echoed this assessment, anticipating a prolonged period of deliberate ambiguity designed to undermine the agreement through military force on the ground.“Netanyahu and the government coalition see accepting the agreement as a political and electoral setback because it preserves the Palestinians’ principle of the right to resist, prevents displacement, and opens the door to rebuilding Gaza,” al-Hila told Al Jazeera.Consequently, Israel’s refusal to formalise its position means the critical 14-day negotiation period for implementation protocols remains entirely frozen, he added.Administering ruinsThe Israeli military also refuses to withdraw from the first “Yellow Line” area, a territory that constitutes approximately 52 percent of the entire Gaza Strip. It also wants complete freedom of military action across the enclave.The roadmap, conversely, calls for empowering an independent, technocratic Palestinian administration to manage civilian affairs and reconstruction in the enclave. Al-Qarra says that granting Israel operational military freedom renders any Palestinian administration entirely meaningless.“Freedom of Israeli action in Gaza means, in practice, a full occupation. An administrative committee cannot operate in thin air; it needs heavy machinery, open border crossings and a suitable environment to rebuild infrastructure and schools,” al-Qarra said.“If an administrative committee operates in areas under Israeli military control, it will be viewed by the people as nothing more than a collaborating militia.”Diplomatic isolationIsrael has also lodged formal objections against the participation of Qatar and Turkiye in the verification mechanisms of the roadmap and demanded their exclusion from the oversight process. contentParagraphs.zh: 自上周宣布巴勒斯坦飞地“停火”第二阶段路线图以来，以色列军队加强了在加沙地带的军事行动。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普称哈马斯接受加沙协议是迈向安全与稳定的里程碑式的一步。在加沙，现实却大不相同，周六至少有 19 名巴勒斯坦人在以色列袭击中丧生，使周末死亡人数达到 26 人，其中包括妇女和儿童。尽管哈马斯同意由于分阶段裁军，以色列政府表示对该计划存在“严重的安全担忧”，并且以色列政界人士对该协议表示强烈抵制。对加沙的持续轰炸导致以色列继续违反十月的“停火”协议，这可能会威胁到特朗普的和平计划，并加剧飞地巴勒斯坦人本已严峻的人道主义局势。这与华盛顿所宣扬的外交进展形成鲜明对比。旨在管理战后加沙的和平委员会和国际稳定部队（ISF）宣布达成一项协议，根据详细的15点路线图实施下一阶段的“停火”。虽然哈马斯正式接受了该文件，但人们质疑巴勒斯坦各派是否会因以色列对加沙的持续袭击而最终退出。驻加沙的巴勒斯坦政治分析人士埃亚德·卡拉（Eyad al-Qarra）告诉半岛电视台，这一步骤将是卡拉说：“仍然希望各派别不会达到这个阶段。否则，人们担心代价会更高，因为以色列会利用这一点对加沙发动更广泛的战争。对于各派别来说，至关重要的是不要给以色列任何借口或借口，让以色列看起来双方都对失败负有同样的责任。” 武器借口 以色列政府并没有接受路线图，而是积极努力以色列媒体报道称，政府要求哈马斯彻底解除武装，并将武器移交给西方国家。他们还坚称，没有任何巴勒斯坦实体在管理解除武装进程中发挥作用。总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡办公室发言人多伦·斯皮尔曼表示，在哈马斯完全非军事化之前，以色列军队不会撤军，这使这一进程进一步复杂化。卡拉说：“哈马斯和其他派系今天的首要任务是救济民众，而不是恢复武器或军事车间。”选举策略专家指出，内塔尼亚胡在加沙问题上的不透明立场背后有根深蒂固的国内政治算计，特别是考虑到大选将于10月举行。以色列事务专家姆塔内斯·谢哈德(Mtanes Shehadeh)指出，政府将加沙谅解严格视为一种战术策略。 Shehadeh 表示：“以色列在加沙城实施饥饿和围困，并在没有明确宣布拒绝路线图的情况下，阻碍协议第二阶段的任何实际进展。”2026 年 8 月 2 日，巴勒斯坦居民在以色列夜间袭击加沙城的一套公寓中尽其所能地抢救。谢哈德补充道：“本杰明·内塔尼亚胡政府将继续实行拖延、逃避和破坏政策，直到 10 月 27 日以色列选举之日，因为任何认真执行商定的路线图都将导致内塔尼亚胡的选举受到损害。”阿尔希拉告诉半岛电视台：“内塔尼亚胡和政府联盟认为接受该协议是政治和选举方面的挫折，因为它保留了巴勒斯坦人抵抗权利的原则，防止流离失所，并为重建加沙打开了大门。”他补充说，因此，以色列拒绝正式确定其立场意味着执行协议关键的 14 天谈判期仍然完全冻结。军方还拒绝从第一个“黄线”地区撤军，该地区约占整个加沙地带的 52%。它还希望在整个飞地采取完全的军事行动自由。相反，路线图呼吁授权一个独立的、技术官僚的巴勒斯坦政府来管理飞地的民事事务和重建。卡拉表示，给予以色列军事行动自由会使任何巴勒斯坦政府完全毫无意义。“以色列在加沙的行动自由实际上意味着全面占领。行政委员会不能凭空运作；它需要重型机械、开放的过境点以及重建基础设施和学校的合适环境，”卡拉说。“如果一个行政委员会在以色列军事控制下的地区运作，人们会认为它只不过是一个合作的民兵。”还正式反对卡塔尔和土耳其参与路线图核查机制，并要求将其排除在监督程序之外。卡拉将此解读为企图剥夺巴勒斯坦人的权利

articles.title: Almost £200,000 of fuel stolen from UK forecourts every day since Iran war began
articles.summary: Incidents of fuel being taken without payment have risen by a fifth in five months, according to industry analysis.
articles.titleZh: 自伊朗战争开始以来，英国前院每天有近 20 万英镑的燃料被盗
articles.summaryZh: 根据行业分析，五个月内无偿取走燃油的事件增加了五分之一。

contentParagraphs.en: UK drivers have stolen almost £200,000 of fuel from petrol stations on average every day since the Iran war broke out and sent prices soaring, according to industry analysis.Incidents of fuel being taken from forecourts without payment have risen by a fifth in the five months since 28 February, figures from Forecourt Eye suggest.The conflict in the Middle East severely disrupted oil supplies across the region, triggering a rise in wholesale prices and subsequent increase in costs at the pump in the UK.Forecourt Eye said the value of the stolen fuel is estimated to have risen by 48% compared with the five months before the war - to reach an estimated daily average of £194,000.The fuel theft prevention company added petrol stations are reporting an increase in "abuse, intimidation and violence from frustrated customers".The figures are based on a representative sample of 550 forecourts, comparing the five months prior to the outbreak with the five months after it started, and extrapolated to the UK's 8,359 forecourts.The number of incidents recorded at the forecourts in the sample equates to 2,872 daily incidents on average at forecourts across the UK in the months after war began, up from around 2,400.They include people driving off without an attempt to pay, and people claiming they have no way to pay after filling their vehicle.The volume of stolen fuel rose by 24% - up from an estimated 87,000 litres to 108,900 litres a day across all forecourts.In response, Forecourt Eye said it would partner with facial recognition company Facewatch to offer more than 2,000 retailers free access to crime reporting technology from the autumn.

articles.title: Iran denies Trump's claim that new talks will begin on Monday
articles.summary: While Iran denies that talks with the US are taking place, it is currently in negotiations with Oman over Strait of Hormuz access.
articles.titleZh: 伊朗否认特朗普关于周一开始新会谈的说法
articles.summaryZh: 虽然伊朗否认正在与美国进行谈判，但目前正在与阿曼就霍尔木兹海峡的通行问题进行谈判。

contentParagraphs.en: Iran has denied Donald Trump's claim that new talks on ending the conflict would begin on Monday, after the US president called off what he said would have been "massive" strikes on the country.Speaking on board Air Force One on Sunday, he said Iran "knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming", adding: "We're talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon."In an earlier post on Truth Social, Trump said he had been asked by Iran and US allies in the Middle East to "hold off" as the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed.But on Monday Iran's foreign ministry denied they were negotiating with the US, or that there were any plans to do so. Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei added that Tehran was negotiating with Oman to reach "an understanding over a path to ensure the security of shipping passage through the Strait of Hormuz".Earlier talks between the US and Iran have been facilitated through mediators.Trump has repeatedly vowed that a negotiated end to the war is near, only for tit-for-tat strikes to resume.In his remarks on Air Force One, Trump declined to outline a deadline for a deal to be struck with Tehran, adding: "We'll just see how it is. We're ready to go anytime we want... I'm not looking to kill people."The US president did specify where the talks on Monday would be held or who would attend.Trump added that Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman - as well as US partners such as the United Arab Emirates and Qatar - had urged him against conducting strikes over the weekend."We were all set to go," Trump said. "The reason they asked is [that] they think there's a deal," he said. "There's a deal on Hormuz, and there will be a deal on the nuclear."Global oil prices fell on Monday morning in Asia trading after Trump's announcement. Brent Crude oil was down by 4.5% at $83.98 (£62.26), while US-traded oil was 4.6% lower at $80.74 (£59.85).Energy prices have fluctuated since the conflict started on 28 February as traders reacted to disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Around 20% of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) usually flows through the strait.Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency denied that Tehran had asked the US to hold off on further military action, saying Trump's claims were "nothing but a new lie".During his remarks on Air Force One, Trump said that the planned strikes would have been "the biggest attack since World War Two", and could have derailed prospects of a negotiated end to the months-long war.Trump declined to answer if he had been planning to strike Iranian energy infrastructure, which international law experts have said could constitute a war crime.Iran's acting Defence Minister Majid Ibn al-Reza earlier said Tehran viewed every threat from its adversaries as "real and credible" even if it formed part of psychological warfare."We will neither be caught off guard nor remain passive," he added.The US president has previously issued apocalyptic warnings to Tehran, only to subsequently insist that diplomacy was being given a chance.In his post on Saturday, he said the US was "locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran, at levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II".But he added cancelling the attack would be "for the future benefit of the world and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran".Back on 7 April, the US president warned that "a whole civilisation will die tonight" if Iran refused to engage in peace talks. At the time, he also threatened to destroy civilian infrastructure and power plants.That threat did result in historic face-to-face talks in Pakistan, led by Vice-President JD Vance. However, those negotiations did not result in a deal.The Trump administration has also been largely dismissive of data showing the war - and its economic impact - are broadly unpopular with Americans, including with many Republicans.Polls showing widespread dissatisfaction with the handling of the war have prompted alarm among some conservative strategists ahead of the coming November midterms.With additional reporting from Peter Hoskins.
contentParagraphs.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普声称，在美国总统取消了他所说的对该国的“大规模”袭击后，伊朗将在周一开始关于结束冲突的新谈判。周日，他在空军一号上发表讲话时表示，伊朗“知道袭击的严重程度，因为他们看到了袭击的形成”，并补充道：“我们正在以谈判的形式与他们交谈。明天下午开始。”特朗普在《真相社会》早些时候的一篇文章中表示，伊朗和美国在中东的盟友向他提出了要求。由于协议的“边界”已达成一致，东方“推迟”。但伊朗外交部周一否认他们正在与美国进行谈判，也否认有任何这样做的计划。发言人埃斯梅尔·巴格海补充说，德黑兰正在与阿曼进行谈判，以“就确保霍尔木兹海峡航运安全的路径达成谅解”。美国和伊朗之间的早期谈判是通过调解人促成的。特朗普一再发誓，通过谈判结束战争即将结束，只是为了恢复针锋相对的打击。在空军一号上的讲话中，特朗普拒绝概述达成协议的最后期限特朗普补充说，沙特阿拉伯王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼以及阿拉伯联合酋长国和卡塔尔等美国合作伙伴敦促他不要在周末发动袭击。“我们已经准备好出发了。” “他们询问的原因是他们认为达成协议，”他说。 “在霍尔木兹海峡达成协议，在核问题上也将达成协议。” 特朗普宣布这一消息后，全球油价周一上午在亚洲交易时段下跌。布伦特原油下跌 4.5%，至 83.98 美元（62.26 英镑），而美国交易的石油下跌 4.6%，至 80.74 美元（59.85 英镑）。自 2 月 28 日冲突开始以来，由于交易商对霍尔木兹海峡航运中断做出反应，能源价格一直波动。世界上大约20%的原油和液化天然气（LNG）通常流经该海峡。伊朗半官方的迈赫尔通讯社否认德黑兰要求美国推迟采取进一步的军事行动，称特朗普的说法“只不过是一个新的谎言”。特朗普在空军一号上发表讲话时表示，计划中的袭击将是“第二次世界大战以来最大规模的袭击”，并可能破坏通过谈判结束伊朗核问题的前景。特朗普拒绝回答他是否计划袭击伊朗能源基础设施，国际法专家称这可能构成战争罪。伊朗代理国防部长马吉德·伊本·礼萨早些时候表示，德黑兰认为来自对手的每一个威胁都是“真实可信的”，即使它是心理战的一部分。“我们既不会措手不及，也不会保持被动，”他补充道。随后坚称，这是给了外交一次机会。在周六的帖子中，他表示，美国“已经上膛，准备好以二战以来从未有过的军事恐怖、力量和力量对抗伊朗伊斯兰共和国”。但他补充说，取消袭击将是“为了世界的未来利益，同样也是为了一个成功和繁荣的伊朗的生存”。早在 4 月 7 日，美国总统就警告说，如果伊朗拒绝进行和平谈判，“整个文明今晚将消亡”。当时，他还威胁要摧毁民用基础设施和发电厂。这一威胁确实导致在巴基斯坦副总统 JD 万斯的主持下举行了历史性的面对面会谈。然而，这些谈判并未达成协议。特朗普政府在很大程度上也对显示这场战争及其经济影响普遍不受美国人（包括许多共和党人）欢迎的数据不屑一顾。民意调查显示，人们对战争的处理方式普遍不满，这在即将到来的 11 月中期选举之前引起了一些保守派战略家的警惕。彼得·霍斯金斯的补充报道。

articles.title: This lawyer believes in second chances. Now AI is providing a boost
articles.summary: Tens of millions of Americans have criminal records that can be barriers to employment. An AI-powered app is helping those eligible to expunge their records at a pace not seen before.
articles.titleZh: 这位律师相信第二次机会。现在人工智能正在提供推动力
articles.summaryZh: 数以千万计的美国人有可能成为就业障碍的犯罪记录。一款人工智能应用程序正在帮助那些有资格的人以前所未有的速度删除他们的记录。

contentParagraphs.en: Noella Sudbury is the founder of Rasa Legal, a startup that is using artificial intelligence to help tens of thousands of people seal or expunge their criminal records.
contentParagraphs.zh: 诺埃拉·萨德伯里 (Noella Sudbury) 是 Rasa Legal 的创始人，这家初创公司正在利用人工智能帮助数以万计的人封存或删除他们的犯罪记录。

contentParagraphs.en: Meredith Rizzo for NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 的梅雷迪思·里佐

contentParagraphs.en: Meredith Rizzo for NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 的梅雷迪思·里佐

contentParagraphs.en: Stay up to date with our Up First newsletter sent every weekday morning.
contentParagraphs.zh: 请随时关注我们每个工作日早上发送的 Up First 时事通讯。

contentParagraphs.en: Since her days as a public defender in Utah, Noella Sudbury has been obsessed with solving a problem: How do you help someone with a criminal record get a job?
contentParagraphs.zh: 自从在犹他州担任公设辩护人以来，诺埃拉·萨德伯里就一直痴迷于解决一个问题：如何帮助有犯罪记录的人找到工作？

contentParagraphs.en: Bottom line: It's really hard.
contentParagraphs.zh: 底线：这真的很难。

contentParagraphs.en: Sudbury had grown frustrated seeing so many people dedicate themselves to changing their lives but still fail to secure housing or work once background checks were run.
contentParagraphs.zh: 萨德伯里看到这么多人致力于改变自己的生活，但在背景调查后仍然无法获得住房或工作，这让萨德伯里感到沮丧。

contentParagraphs.en: A history of arrests involving drugs or retail theft — the most common offenses — can scare off employers.
contentParagraphs.zh: 涉及毒品或零售盗窃（最常见的犯罪行为）的逮捕历史可能会吓跑雇主。

contentParagraphs.en: "They make assumptions that someone's dishonest, or they're going to steal," she says. "We should have a presumption of innocence, but unfortunately, you see something that scares you, and you make a subjective decision."
contentParagraphs.zh: “他们假设某人不诚实，或者他们会偷窃，”她说。 “我们应该有无罪推定，但不幸的是，你看到一些让你害怕的东西，然后你就做出了主观决定。”

contentParagraphs.en: Research has shown that, in fact, people who have gotten their criminal records cleared are less likely than the general public to commit a crime.
contentParagraphs.zh: 研究表明，事实上，清除犯罪记录的人犯罪的可能性低于普通公众。

contentParagraphs.en: Back in 2018, Sudbury began running expungement clinics in Salt Lake County. Every time, hundreds of people would show up, some with their children in tow, others driving hours to get there. Every time, by 9 p.m., Sudbury was turning people away, telling them the lawyers had to go home.
contentParagraphs.zh: 早在 2018 年，萨德伯里就开始在盐湖县经营清除诊所。每次都会有数百人出现，其中一些人带着孩子，另一些人则驱车数小时到达那里。每次到晚上 9 点，萨德伯里就会把人们拒之门外，告诉他们律师必须回家。

contentParagraphs.en: The process was laborious. It would take lawyers up to an hour just to piece together what was on someone's record to figure out if they were eligible for expungement under state law.
contentParagraphs.zh: 过程很辛苦。律师需要花费长达一个小时的时间来拼凑某人的记录，以确定他们是否有资格根据州法律进行删除。

contentParagraphs.en: Sudbury recalls one man who arrived with a rolling suitcase filled with all kinds of documents.
contentParagraphs.zh: 萨德伯里回忆说，一名男子带着一个装满各种文件的拉杆箱抵达。

contentParagraphs.en: "The amount of paper was so voluminous that he couldn't carry it all. And I'm like, 'This is nuts because all of this could live in a digital format,'" she says.
contentParagraphs.zh: “纸张数量如此之大，他无法全部携带。我想，‘这太疯狂了，因为所有这些都可以以数字格式存在，’”她说。

contentParagraphs.en: That led to an idea. What if she could access all of the information the background check companies use?
contentParagraphs.zh: 这引发了一个想法。如果她可以访问背景调查公司使用的所有信息怎么办？

contentParagraphs.en: "Could I build an app? Could I use technology to reduce my time?" she remembers thinking. "I just believed it was possible."
contentParagraphs.zh: “我可以开发一个应用程序吗？我可以使用技术来减少我的时间吗？”她记得当时在想。 “我只是相信这是可能的。”

contentParagraphs.en: Speeding up record clearance to help secure jobs
contentParagraphs.zh: 加快记录清理速度以帮助确保就业

contentParagraphs.en: Now, amid a barrage of news about AI-related layoffs at tech companies like Uber and Meta and widespread fear that AI will decimate all kinds of entry-level jobs, from paralegals to junior accountants to customer support, Sudbury is leaning heavily into AI to help people get jobs — by speeding up the record clearance process for those who are eligible.
contentParagraphs.zh: 现在，随着 Uber 和 Meta 等科技公司与人工智能相关的裁员消息层出不穷，人们普遍担心人工智能将大量减少从律师助理到初级会计师再到客户支持等各种初级工作岗位，萨德伯里正在大力依靠人工智能来帮助人们找到工作——通过加快符合条件的人的记录审批流程。

contentParagraphs.en: The tech team at her startup Rasa Legal has brought her idea to life, building an app that can determine whether someone is eligible for expungement in just three minutes. AI has also cut the time it takes Rasa's lawyers to file a petition for expungement by more than half.
contentParagraphs.zh: 她的初创公司 Rasa Legal 的技术团队将她的想法变为现实，开发了一款应用程序，可以在短短三分钟内确定某人是否有资格删除。 AI 还将 Rasa 的律师提交删除申请的时间缩短了一半以上。

contentParagraphs.en: Rasa Legal's website currently allows users in three states to determine in about three minutes whether they are eligible for expungement.
contentParagraphs.zh: Rasa Legal 的网站目前允许三个州的用户在大约三分钟内确定他们是否有资格删除。

contentParagraphs.en: "What that means for me as a lawyer is that we can scale our impact far beyond what would be possible if we were relying on human beings," she says.
contentParagraphs.zh: “作为一名律师，这对我来说意味着我们可以扩大我们的影响力，远远超出我们依靠人类所能达到的程度，”她说。

contentParagraphs.en: Sudbury estimates that legal aid organizations doing record clearance work might be able to serve a few hundred people each year. Since launching its app in 2022, Rasa has helped clear the records of 34,000 people in three states where it's currently operating: Utah, Arizona and Pennsylvania.
contentParagraphs.zh: 萨德伯里估计，从事记录清理工作的法律援助组织每年可能能够为数百人提供服务。自 2022 年推出应用程序以来，Rasa 已帮助清除其目前运营的三个州的 34,000 人的记录：犹他州、亚利桑那州和宾夕法尼亚州。

contentParagraphs.en: Across the country, Sudbury knows it could help potentially millions more.
contentParagraphs.zh: 萨德伯里知道，在全国范围内，它可能会帮助数百万人。

contentParagraphs.en: Precise numbers are hard to come by, but it's long been estimated that more than 70 million adults in the U.S. have some kind of criminal record, a number extrapolated from FBI and state data. These include felonies, misdemeanors and, in some cases, arrests without convictions — all things that can show up on background checks.
contentParagraphs.zh: 准确的数字很难获得，但长期以来据联邦调查局和各州数据推断，美国有超过 7000 万成年人有某种犯罪记录。其中包括重罪、轻罪，在某些情况下，还包括未经定罪的逮捕——所有这些都可能出现在背景调查中。

contentParagraphs.en: In a 2020 paper, professor Colleen Chien of the University of California, Berkeley, School of Law, estimated that at least 20 million people could partially or fully clear their records under existing law but have not done so. She calls this the "second chance expungement gap."
contentParagraphs.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校法学院教授 Colleen Chien 在 2020 年的一篇论文中估计，至少有 2000 万人可以根据现行法律部分或全部清除自己的记录，但尚未这样做。她称之为“第二次机会消除差距”。

contentParagraphs.en: "The criminalization of poverty"
contentParagraphs.zh: “将贫困定为犯罪”

contentParagraphs.en: Virginia Mireles knew she looked terrible on paper.
contentParagraphs.zh: 维吉尼亚·米雷莱斯知道她在纸面上看起来很糟糕。

contentParagraphs.en: "Five felony records, all due to my drug addiction," she says.
contentParagraphs.zh: “五项重罪记录，全都是因为我的毒瘾，”她说。

contentParagraphs.en: Mireles' story is like so many others seeking help from Rasa. She grew up in poverty in Tucson, Ariz., and began using heroin at 14.
contentParagraphs.zh: 米雷莱斯的故事就像许多其他向拉莎寻求帮助的人一样。她在亚利桑那州图森市的贫困家庭中长大，14 岁时开始吸食海洛因。

contentParagraphs.en: "Unfortunately, an older uncle decided that was his way of taking care of me," she says.
contentParagraphs.zh: “不幸的是，一位年长的叔叔认为这是他照顾我的方式，”她说。

contentParagraphs.en: She was incarcerated for the first time at 24. For more than two decades, she cycled in and out of the Arizona prison system. While behind bars, she says, you think a lot about how you're going to change. But when you get out?
contentParagraphs.zh: 她 24 岁时第一次入狱。二十多年来，她骑自行车进出亚利桑那州监狱系统。她说，在监狱里，你会经常思考如何改变。但是当你出去的时候呢？

contentParagraphs.en: "You can't rent a house under your own name, and you can't find a job that's going to help you support your family," she says. "So now you just feel terrible about yourself because your family's looking at you like — 'I thought you were going to be different.'"
contentParagraphs.zh: “你不能用自己的名字租房子，你也找不到一份可以帮助你养家糊口的工作，”她说。 “所以现在你对自己感觉很糟糕，因为你的家人看着你就像——‘我以为你会有所不同。’”

contentParagraphs.en: Virginia Mireles spent decades grappling with addiction and cycling in and out of the Arizona prison system. After a collective 17 years incarcerated, she used Rasa to expunge her criminal record and now works with the company, talking potential clients through the record clearance process.
contentParagraphs.zh: 维吉尼亚·米雷莱斯（Virginia Mireles）花了数十年的时间与毒瘾作斗争，并骑自行车进出亚利桑那州监狱系统。在集体被监禁 17 年后，她利用 Rasa 消除了自己的犯罪记录，现在与该公司合作，与潜在客户讨论记录清除流程。

contentParagraphs.en: Meredith Rizzo for NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 的梅雷迪思·里佐

contentParagraphs.en: Meredith Rizzo for NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 的梅雷迪思·里佐

contentParagraphs.en: Sudbury, whose mother grew up poor in rural Utah, calls this "the criminalization of poverty." Too often, she says, the root causes of people's problems — mental health, trauma, substance use and poverty — go unaddressed.
contentParagraphs.zh: 萨德伯里的母亲在犹他州农村长大，她的母亲很穷，她称这是“对贫困的刑事定罪”。她说，人们问题的根源——心理健康、创伤、药物滥用和贫困——往往没有得到解决。

contentParagraphs.en: "What I saw when I became a public defender was the faces of my mother's family members," she says. "We were using a broken system to punish those people instead of treating them for what I saw as largely health issues."
contentParagraphs.zh: “当我成为一名公设辩护人时，我看到的是我母亲家人的面孔，”她说。 “我们使用一个破碎的系统来惩罚这些人，而不是针对我认为主要是健康问题的人进行治疗。”

contentParagraphs.en: Expungement as an economic tool
contentParagraphs.zh: 消除作为一种经济工具
