contentParagraphs.zh: 大多数州允许封存或删除一些犯罪记录，包括轻罪和非暴力重罪，只要印度人

articles.title: Rare photos of ex-Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi give her family hope
articles.summary: Kim Aris, son of Aung San Suu Kyi, told NPR that photographs of his mother meeting a foreign official gave him "a reason to hope" for the first time since the military coup that ousted her in 2021.
articles.titleZh: 缅甸前领导人昂山素季的罕见照片给她的家人带来希望
articles.summaryZh: 昂山素季的儿子金·阿里斯 (Kim Aris) 告诉 NPR，自 2021 年军事政变推翻她母亲以来，他母亲会见外国官员的照片第一次给了他“希望的理由”。

contentParagraphs.en: In this photo released by Myanmar President Office on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, Myanmar's ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi, left, shakes hands with Arnaud de Baecque, resident representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross, during their meeting in Naypyitaw, Myanmar.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在缅甸总统办公室于 2026 年 8 月 3 日星期一发布的这张照片中，缅甸被罢黜的领导人昂山素季（左）在缅甸内比都举行会议期间与红十字国际委员会常驻代表阿诺·德巴克握手。

contentParagraphs.en: Myanmar President Office/AP
contentParagraphs.zh: 缅甸总统府/美联社

contentParagraphs.en: Myanmar President Office/AP
contentParagraphs.zh: 缅甸总统府/美联社

contentParagraphs.en: CHIANG MAI — The son of Aung San Suu Kyi has told NPR that rare new pictures of the detained former Myanmar leader released by the country's military have given them renewed hope over her well-being.
contentParagraphs.zh: 清迈——昂山素季的儿子告诉美国国家公共广播电台，该国军方发布了这位被拘留的前缅甸领导人罕见的新照片，让他们对她的健康重新燃起了希望。

contentParagraphs.en: Kim Aris, the younger son of Suu Kyi, said photographs released Monday of his mother meeting the head of an international humanitarian group gave him "a reason to hope" for the first time since the military coup that ousted her in 2021.
contentParagraphs.zh: 昂山素季的小儿子金·阿里斯 (Kim Aris) 表示，周一发布的他母亲会见国际人道主义组织负责人的照片让他自 2021 年军事政变推翻她以来第一次“有理由抱有希望”。

contentParagraphs.en: After years of enforced isolation, Suu Kyi met with Arnaud de Baecque, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)'s resident representative in Myanmar, in the capital Naypyitaw on Monday, according to government spokeswoman Khine Khine Soe, who announced the meeting via Telegram. The ICRC confirmed in a statement it took place and "included the opportunity" to speak in private with her.
contentParagraphs.zh: 据通过 Telegram 宣布会面消息的缅甸政府发言人 Khine Khine Soe 称，经过多年的强制隔离，昂山素季周一在首都内比都会见了红十字国际委员会驻缅甸代表阿诺·德巴克 (Arnaud de Baecque)。红十字国际委员会在一份声明中证实了此事的发生，并“提供了”与她私下交谈的机会。

contentParagraphs.en: Photographs released alongside the announcement show Suu Kyi shaking hands with de Baecque in a sparsely furnished, wood-paneled room.
contentParagraphs.zh: 与公告一起发布的照片​​显示，昂山素季在一间陈设稀疏、镶有木板的房间里与德巴克握手。

contentParagraphs.en: "I hope this is the beginning of transparency, humanitarian access and, ultimately, my mother's freedom," said Aris – who is based in London – in an email to NPR. "But hope is not proof, and one meeting cannot answer the questions my family has lived with since the coup."
contentParagraphs.zh: “我希望这是透明度、人道主义准入以及最终我母亲自由的开始，”居住在伦敦的阿里斯在给美国国家公共广播电台的电子邮件中说。 “但希望并不能证明，一次会议无法回答我的家人自政变以来一直面临的问题。”

contentParagraphs.en: Reports by Myanmar's military regarding Suu Kyi have long been treated with scepticism, as she has been held incommunicado since her arrest – a move that has silenced the most popular politician in the country of 55 million people. Suu Kyi won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1991.
contentParagraphs.zh: 缅甸军方有关昂山素季的报道长期以来一直受到怀疑，因为她被捕后一直被单独监禁 — — 这一举动让这位在这个拥有 5500 万人口的国家最受欢迎的政治家噤声。昂山素季于1991年获得诺贝尔和平奖。

contentParagraphs.en: Two additional images appear to be from an earlier occasion: Suu Kyi's 81st birthday in June. One image shows her cutting a pink cake inscribed "Happy Birthday Aunty Suu, 19.6.2026". In those images, Suu Kyi is wearing a different outfit, with a clothes rack and storage boxes visible.
contentParagraphs.zh: 另外两张图片似乎来自较早的场合：昂山素季 6 月的 81 岁生日。一张照片显示她正在切一个粉红色的蛋糕，上面写着“苏阿姨生日快乐，2026 年 6 月 19 日”。在这些照片中，昂山素季穿着不同的衣服，可以看到衣架和储物箱。

contentParagraphs.en: In this photo released by Myanmar President Office on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, Myanmar ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi cuts a birthday cake during her meeting with Arnaud de Baecque, resident representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross, in Naypyitaw, Myanmar.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在缅甸总统办公室于 2026 年 8 月 3 日星期一发布的这张照片中，缅甸被罢黜的领导人昂山素季在缅甸内比都会见红十字国际委员会驻地代表阿诺·德巴克时切生日蛋糕。

contentParagraphs.en: Myanmar President Office/AP
contentParagraphs.zh: 缅甸总统府/美联社

contentParagraphs.en: Myanmar President Office/AP
contentParagraphs.zh: 缅甸总统府/美联社

contentParagraphs.en: Aris and Myanmar democracy activists have spent years demanding proof his mother is alive and well. Aris said the ICRC had not yet briefed him on her health or the meeting, despite the ICRC saying such visits provide the opportunity "to exchange news with their families". The ICRC did not respond to NPR's questions immediately.
contentParagraphs.zh: 阿里斯和缅甸民主活动人士多年来一直要求证明他的母亲还活着并且身体健康。阿里斯表示，红十字国际委员会尚未向他通报她的健康状况或会面情况，尽管红十字国际委员会表示此类探视提供了“与家人交换消息”的机会。红十字国际委员会没有立即回应国家公共广播电台的问题。

contentParagraphs.en: "It gave me hope, but I remain cautious," Aris said of the photographs, calling them "deeply emotional". "Now that hope must be matched by transparency, compassion and meaningful action," he added.
contentParagraphs.zh: “它给了我希望，但我仍然保持谨慎，”阿里斯谈到这些照片时说，称它们“充满情感”。 “现在，这种希望必须与透明度、同情心和有意义的行动相匹配，”他补充道。

contentParagraphs.en: The meeting comes as pressure builds on Myanmar's military-backed government, including from fellow Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) members, to grant international access to Suu Kyi. Since the 2021 coup – which triggered a civil war that has killed an estimated 100,000 people and displaced millions – no foreign leader or envoy had publicly met her.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这次会议召开之际，缅甸军方支持的政府面临越来越大的压力，其中包括来自东南亚国家联盟（ASEAN）其他成员国的压力，要求其允许国际社会接触昂山素季。 2021 年政变引发了一场内战，造成约 10 万人死亡，数百万人流离失所，自此以来，没有任何外国领导人或特使公开会见她。

contentParagraphs.en: In late April, following a military-orchestrated election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as president, authorities said Suu Kyi had been moved to house arrest.
contentParagraphs.zh: 4月下旬，在军事策划的选举中军政府领导人敏昂莱当选总统后，当局表示昂山素季已被软禁。

contentParagraphs.en: Thomas Kean, a senior consultant on Myanmar at the International Crisis Group, said the military likely allowed the meeting between Suu Kyi and the ICRC delegation because Min Aung Hlaing wants Myanmar welcomed back into ASEAN, whose foreign ministers have discussed benchmarks for the bloc's stalled peace plan.
contentParagraphs.zh: 国际危机组织缅甸问题高级顾问托马斯·基恩表示，军方可能允许昂山素季与红十字国际委员会代表会面，因为敏昂莱希望欢迎缅甸重返东盟，东盟外长们已经讨论了该集团陷入僵局的和平计划的基准。

contentParagraphs.en: "Min Aung Hlaing is just about to head to Thailand, which has been pushing hard for normalisation with Myanmar and will likely cite this as a positive step," Kean told NPR. But he cautioned it does not signal progress toward ending the conflict, "no matter how hard Naypyitaw or its allies in the region try to spin it."
contentParagraphs.zh: 基恩告诉美国国家公共广播电台：“敏昂莱即将前往泰国，泰国一直在努力推动与缅甸关系正常化，并可能会将此视为积极的一步。”但他警告说，这并不意味着结束冲突取得了进展，“无论内比都或其在该地区的盟友多么努力地试图扭转冲突”。

contentParagraphs.en: At most, he said, "it shows Aung San Suu Kyi is alive and that she appears to be in reasonable health."
contentParagraphs.zh: 他说，最多“这表明昂山素季还活着，而且她的健康状况似乎还不错。”

contentParagraphs.en: Repression inside Myanmar continues. In July, a Yangon court sentenced Saw Naing, a former lawmaker, to three years in prison for marking Suu Kyi's birthday with a religious ceremony and calling for her release.
contentParagraphs.zh: 缅甸境内的镇压仍在继续。 7月，仰光一家法院判处前议员苏奈三年监禁，原因是她以宗教仪式庆祝昂山素季的生日，并呼吁释放她。

contentParagraphs.en: Nay Phone Latt, spokesperson for the anti-junta National Unity Government, told NPR that armed opposition forces would "continue to fight until the objectives of the revolution are achieved", including the release of Suu Kyi.
contentParagraphs.zh: 反军政府民族团结政府发言人内·丰拉特 (Nay Phone Latt) 告诉美国国家公共广播电台，武装反对派武装将“继续战斗，直到实现革命目标”，包括释放昂山素季。

articles.title: Bedbugs, bad Wi-Fi: Federal workers say forced summer relocations have been chaos
articles.summary: Federal agencies are rushing to move hundreds of workers into new buildings. Employees say the moves are significantly disrupting their work.
articles.titleZh: 臭虫、糟糕的 Wi-Fi：联邦工作人员称强制夏季搬迁很混乱
articles.summaryZh: 联邦机构正忙着将数百名工人转移到新建筑中。员工表示，这些举措严重扰乱了他们的工作。

contentParagraphs.en: Daniel Kim, a structural engineer with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, says uncertainty about the planned relocation of the agency's New York District headquarters has already contributed to the loss of experienced staff.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国陆军工程兵团结构工程师丹尼尔·金表示，该机构纽约地区总部计划搬迁的不确定性已经导致经验丰富的员工流失。

contentParagraphs.en: Shuran Huang for NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 黄舒然

contentParagraphs.en: Shuran Huang for NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 黄舒然

contentParagraphs.en: For more than five decades, NASA occupied several floors of office space in Manhattan rented from Columbia University, where employees researched how warming temperatures could alter weather and climate. Last year, the Trump administration abruptly forced all NASA employees out of that office to save money, officials said. This year, it's asking employees to move into new spaces. But the government continues to pay millions annually in rent for the old space.
contentParagraphs.zh: 五十多年来，美国宇航局占据了曼哈顿从哥伦比亚大学租来的几层办公空间，员工们在那里研究气温升高如何改变天气和气候。官员们表示，去年，特朗普政府突然强迫所有 NASA 员工离开该办公室，以节省开支。今年，它要求员工搬到新的办公空间。但政府每年仍继续为旧空间支付数百万美元的租金。

contentParagraphs.en: NASA's move was part of a series of relocations launched by the Trump administration across at least six federal agencies that have continued through the summer. The relocations, agency leaders say, will reduce the government's real estate footprint, cut costs and decentralize operations away from the Washington, D.C. core.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国宇航局的此举是特朗普政府在至少六个联邦机构中发起的一系列搬迁行动的一部分，这些搬迁行动一直持续到整个夏天。该机构领导人表示，搬迁将减少政府的房地产足迹，降低成本，并将业务分散到华盛顿特区的核心地区。

contentParagraphs.en: But moving is costing the government money, an NPR review of public records shows, and federal workers say the relocations have been poorly coordinated and are causing work disruptions. The moves have also violated laws that require Congress to authorize relocations, according to two legal complaints filed in July against federal agencies and against senior leaders in the Trump administration.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但国家公共广播电台对公共记录的审查显示，搬迁需要花费政府资金，联邦工作人员表示，搬迁协调不力，导致工作中断。根据 7 月份针对联邦机构和特朗普政府高级领导人提出的两份法律投诉，这些举措还违反了要求国会授权搬迁的法律。

contentParagraphs.en: NASA used to occupy multiple floors in the Armstrong Hall building at Columbia University. Now those floors are empty, but the government is still paying rent.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国宇航局曾经占据哥伦比亚大学阿姆斯特朗大厅大楼的多个楼层。现在这些楼层已经空了，但政府仍在支付租金。

contentParagraphs.en: Shuran Huang for NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 黄舒然

contentParagraphs.en: Shuran Huang for NPR
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 黄舒然

contentParagraphs.en: "You're not supposed to be doing this," said Steve Gutierrez, a representative with the National Federation of Federal Employees, the union representing U.S. Forest Service workers. "But oversight [in Congress] hasn't done anything about it."
contentParagraphs.zh: “你不应该这样做，”代表美国林务局工人的全国联邦雇员联合会的代表史蒂夫·古铁雷斯说。 “但（国会）的监督并没有对此采取任何行动。”

contentParagraphs.en: Costly leases, buildings with bedbugs, bad Wi-Fi
contentParagraphs.zh: 昂贵的租金、有臭虫的建筑物、糟糕的 Wi-Fi

contentParagraphs.en: NASA employees who were based at Columbia, where they often collaborated on research with faculty, were instructed to report to four new locations spread out across New York City by August, emails reviewed by NPR show. But the federal government has continued to pay more than $2.5 million annually to rent the five, now-empty floors near Columbia, public records reveal. That lease doesn't expire until 2031.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 查阅的电子邮件显示，美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 常驻哥伦比亚的员工经常与哥伦比亚大学的教员合作进行研究，他们被指示在 8 月份之前到纽约市的四个新地点报到。但公共记录显示，联邦政府每年继续支付超过 250 万美元来租用哥伦比亚附近现已空置的五层楼。该租约要到 2031 年才会到期。

contentParagraphs.en: "Now they're paying this extra money for us to have seats so that we can return to office," said a current NASA employee who was told to report to one of the new locations. "It made zero sense."
contentParagraphs.zh: “现在他们支付额外的钱让我们有座位，这样我们就可以返回办公室，”一名现任 NASA 员工说，他被告知要到一个新地点报到。 “这毫无意义。”

contentParagraphs.en: Current federal employees requested that NPR not use their names because they feared retribution for speaking to the media.
contentParagraphs.zh: 现任联邦雇员要求 NPR 不要使用他们的名字，因为他们担心因向媒体发表言论而受到报复。

contentParagraphs.en: Hundreds of employees with the U.S. Forest Service, part of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, are also being affected this summer.
contentParagraphs.zh: 今年夏天，隶属于美国农业部的美国林业局的数百名员工也受到了影响。

contentParagraphs.en: In a budget hearing in Washington in April, Forest Service Chief Tom Schulz said many of the agency's employees would have to move locations to help the agency maximize "value to the American taxpayer." But Schulz said the moves wouldn't happen until after the wildfire season, when many employees who coordinate wildfire response are busiest and federal firefighters' lives are at greatest risk.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在四月于华盛顿举行的预算听证会上，林务局局长汤姆·舒尔茨表示，该机构的许多员工将不得不搬迁地点，以帮助该机构最大限度地“为美国纳税人创造价值”。但舒尔茨表示，这些举措要等到野火季节结束后才会发生，届时许多协调野火应对工作的员工最为忙碌，联邦消防员的生命危险也最大。

contentParagraphs.en: "We do not anticipate moving any of the field personnel in any fashion until after the fire season," said Schulz.
contentParagraphs.zh: 舒尔茨说：“我们预计在火灾季节结束之前不会以任何方式转移任何现场人员。”

contentParagraphs.en: Yet on July 22, as federal firefighters were on high alert as dozens of wildfires were spreading across multiple states, Schulz sent an email to Forest Service staff informing them that the reorganization would begin that week.
contentParagraphs.zh: 然而，7 月 22 日，由于数十起野火在多个州蔓延，联邦消防队员处于高度戒备状态，舒尔茨向林务局工作人员发送了一封电子邮件，通知他们重组将于本周开始。

contentParagraphs.en: When asked why the agency was starting the reorganization during wildfire season, the USDA emailed a statement to NPR that did not answer the question. But the statement confirmed that around 600 employees would receive updated assignments by August 20, and of those, "approximately 75 may involve relocation."
contentParagraphs.zh: 当被问及为什么该机构要在野火季节开始重组时，美国农业部通过电子邮件向 NPR 发送了一份声明，但没有回答这个问题。但声明证实，到 8 月 20 日，大约 600 名员工将收到更新的任务分配，其中“大约 75 名可能涉及调动”。

contentParagraphs.en: "You said you weren't going to do this until end of fire season, and now you're doing [it] in the middle of fire season," Gutierrez said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 古铁雷斯说：“你说过要等到火灾季节结束后才会这样做，但现在却在火灾季节中期这样做。”

contentParagraphs.en: The Washington Metro passes in front of the building in Alexandria, Va. that USDA employees were told they must leave by the end of August.
contentParagraphs.zh: 华盛顿地铁经过弗吉尼亚州亚历山大市的大楼前，美国农业部员工被告知必须在八月底之前离开。

contentParagraphs.en: Other agency leaders have also sent mixed messages. In February, USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins said the agency was moving forward with moving out employees who help administer the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), formerly known as food stamps, from a building in Alexandria, Va. As of June, the government was renting that building from a private company for more than $4 million a year.
contentParagraphs.zh: 其他机构领导人也发出了复杂的信息。今年 2 月，美国农业部部长布鲁克·罗林斯 (Brooke Rollins) 表示，该机构正在着手将帮助管理补充营养援助计划 (SNAP)（以前称为食品券）的员工从弗吉尼亚州亚历山大市的一栋建筑中迁出。截至 6 月，政府正以每年超过 400 万美元的价格从一家私人公司租用该建筑。

contentParagraphs.en: "This is a long overdue move to protect American taxpayer dollars from being wasted on expensive real estate inside the Washington, D.C. area when our government should be closer to the farmers and ranchers we serve," Rollins said in a press release.
contentParagraphs.zh: 罗林斯在一份新闻稿中表示：“这是一项迟来的举措，旨在保护美国纳税人的资金不被浪费在华盛顿特区内昂贵的房地产上，而我们的政府应该更接近我们所服务的农民和牧场主。”

contentParagraphs.en: But the lease in Alexandria doesn't end until 2034, public records show. And while some SNAP employees may be moved to other locations, the employees who were told to move out of Alexandria haven't been directed to relocate near ranches. They've been told to report by the end of August to two buildings, one in Washington and another in Maryland.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但公共记录显示，亚历山大的租约要到 2034 年才会结束。虽然一些 SNAP 员工可能会被转移到其他地点，但被告知搬出亚历山大的员工并没有被指示搬到牧场附近。他们被告知要在八月底之前向两栋大楼报告，一栋位于华盛顿，另一栋位于马里兰州。

contentParagraphs.en: In May, that Maryland location was treated for a bedbug infestation. The agency informed staff it expects the infestation to be fully mitigated by the time new USDA employees arrive. But as of late July, the agency told employees it was still working on the bedbug problem, internal USDA communications reviewed by NPR show.
contentParagraphs.zh: 五月，马里兰州的那个地点接受了臭虫侵扰的治疗。该机构告知工作人员，预计在美国农业部新员工到达时，感染情况将得到完全缓解。但美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 查阅的美国农业部内部通讯显示，截至 7 月底，该机构告诉员工，它仍在解决臭虫问题。

contentParagraphs.en: The USDA did not respond to a list of emailed questions about the bedbugs or its former office lease.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国农业部没有回复有关臭虫或其前办公室租赁的电子邮件问题清单。

contentParagraphs.en: Some USDA employees who used to work in Alexandria were told to move in to the George Washington Carver Center building in Beltsville, Md., where bedbugs were found in May.
contentParagraphs.zh: 一些曾经在亚历山大工作的美国农业部雇员被告知搬进马里兰州贝尔茨维尔的乔治·华盛顿·卡弗中心大楼，那里于五月份发现了臭虫。
